## Purpose

The React Frontend is the primary operator interface for the vQA system. It runs entirely in the browser as a static SPA — there is no server-side rendering. Operators use it to select a Jira ticket, choose a user role, optionally review and edit parsed AC steps, launch a test execution, and watch real-time step-by-step progress via WebSocket streaming (live screenshots, agent reasoning, per-AC step status). During human-in-the-loop (HITL) events the TakeoverPanel replaces the live browser view, offering two intervention modes: Normal HITL (inject browser actions) and Click-to-Teach (auto-capture DOM selectors for KB training). After execution the dashboard shows failure triage, S3 audit reports, session video, and aggregated analytics over configurable time windows.

The frontend communicates exclusively with the vQA Backend through REST calls and a WebSocket stream. It has no direct access to any database, AWS service, or Jira.

## Interfaces

### Outbound REST API (to vQA Backend, port 8000)

API base URL configured via `VITE_API_URL` build-time env var (default: `http://localhost:8000`).

| Purpose | Endpoint | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| Health check | `GET /health` | Called on dashboard load; no auth required |
| Ticket listing | `GET /tickets` | Jira board tickets for selector dropdown (5-min cache in backend) |
| Credential check | `GET /ticket/{id}/credentials` | Pre-flight before run start |
| AC step preview | `GET /preview-steps` | Parse AC steps without starting a run |
| Start run | `POST /execute` | Returns run_id + WS URL |
| Poll run status | `GET /status/{run_id}` | Fallback polling (primary: WebSocket) |
| Cancel run | `POST /run/{run_id}/cancel` | Graceful stop |
| HITL inject | `POST /runs/{run_id}/interact` | Mouse click / keystroke / scroll injection |
| Click-to-Teach | `POST /runs/{run_id}/teach/capture-click` | Element selector auto-detection |
| Teach & persist | `POST /runs/{run_id}/teach` | Save selector + guidance to KB |
| Resume after HITL | `POST /runs/{run_id}/human-takeover/done` | Signal agent to continue |
| Skip AC step | `POST /runs/{run_id}/human-takeover/skip` | Skip stuck step |
| Post to Jira | `POST /run/{run_id}/post-to-jira` | Post triage as Jira comment |
| Analytics | `GET /runs/analytics?days={n}` | Pass rate, cost, top tickets |
| Run history | `GET /runs/history` | Paginated run list |
| Reports archive | `GET /reports` | S3 audit report records |

### Outbound WebSocket (to vQA Backend, port 8000)

WebSocket base URL configured via `VITE_WS_URL` build-time env var (default: `ws://localhost:8000`).

| Path | Hook | Events Handled |
|------|------|---------------|
| `WS /ws/{run_id}` | `useWebSocket` | `step`, `thinking`, `screenshot`, `ac_progress`, `copilot_ready`, `triage`, `completed`, `failed` |

### Environment Configuration

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|----------|---------|---------|
| `VITE_API_URL` | `http://localhost:8000` | Backend REST base URL (injected at Vite build time) |
| `VITE_WS_URL` | `ws://localhost:8000` | Backend WebSocket base URL (injected at Vite build time) |

No sensitive values should appear in the `VITE_*` variables — they are baked into the static JS bundle at build time and visible to browser clients.

## Local Development

```bash
# Install frontend dependencies
cd frontend && npm install

# Start Vite dev server (HMR, port 5173)
cd frontend && npm run dev

# Production build (outputs to frontend/dist/)
cd frontend && npm run build

# Type-check + lint
cd frontend && npm run preview
```

See `memory-bank/techContext.md` § Development Commands for the canonical full list.

For full-stack local development, `./start.sh` starts both the backend (port 8000) and frontend dev server (port 3000 per techContext.md / 5173 per Vite defaults — confirm in `frontend/vite.config.ts`).

## Notes

- **No server-side secrets**: All `VITE_*` config is public (baked into the bundle). Credentials and API keys must never be placed in `VITE_*` variables.
- **Bundle size discipline**: AnalyticsDashboard uses a custom SVG ring chart (no charting library) to keep the bundle lean. Avoid adding heavy dependencies.
- **WebSocket reset safety**: `useWebSocket.resetState()` clears all run state without closing the socket — prevents stale data from a previous ticket bleed into a new selection when the operator switches tickets without a page reload.
- **HITL dual-mode**: TakeoverPanel exposes Normal HITL (direct action injection) and Click-to-Teach (KB training) in a single panel with a mode toggle. Activates when the backend sends `copilot_ready` via WebSocket.
